subject: Food Science
title: Pasteurization
description: A micro-lesson that makes Pasteurization usable.

hook.text: Before pasteurization, milk caused 25% of all food-borne disease outbreaks. Louis Pasteur's 1864 discovery changed food safety.

buildup.text: Pasteurization heats food to a specific temperature for a set time—enough to kill dangerous pathogens without cooking the product.

discovery.text: HTST (High Temperature Short Time): 72°C for 15 seconds. LTLT (Low Temperature Long Time): 63°C for 30 minutes.

twist.text: Pasteurization doesn't sterilize—it reduces pathogen counts to safe levels. That's why pasteurized milk spoils and needs.

climax.text: Juice pasteurization was mandated after E. coli outbreaks from fresh apple cider in the 1990s killed a child.

punchline.text: Heat enough to kill pathogens, not enough to destroy the food.

quiz.question: Why does pasteurized milk still need refrigeration?
options: Pasteurization reduces pathogens to safe levels but doesn't sterilize—some bacteria remain
